I can't make a strong case for buying this one. The brief points to an operator-backed launch with the coin's supply concentrated in a few hands. Its first two minutes after graduation show about 901 SOL of buying from 12 buyers, with the top five buyers taking 99.96% of it. The curve data shows bundle_share and top3_share at 1.0, and the sell-to-buy ratio is 0.002, so almost nothing was sold early.

The one honest point in its favor is that the coin is alive and held its level over the last 15 minutes, with net inflow of 3.85 SOL and a +0.75% return. Buying was also active enough, at 15 buyers and 15 SOL of buys.

But that recent stability is weak evidence of organic demand. Sellers (10) and sell volume (11.19 SOL) were nearly as large as buyers, so the recent flow is churn among a small group, not broadening interest. The 137x return over 30 minutes is a launch spike, not a base to build on, and the drawdown from the 30-minute high is zero only because the high is recent. memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: insider distribution by the operator. This is an OPERATOR-class coin: bundle_share 1.0, top3_share 1.0, and 901 SOL bought in the first two minutes from just 12 buyers, with top-5 buyers holding 99.96% of that flow. The operator has a massive cost basis far below the current price (return_30_min +137x), so there is every incentive to sell into any bid we provide.

Last 15 minutes show the sell pressure building: 11.19 SOL sold versus 15.03 bought, with 10 sellers, and the sell_to_buy ratio of 0.002 in the launch window only reflects early flow. Pool depth is about 1,000 SOL, so a $20 ticket will move little, and the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost means we need a sustained rise just to break even. Drawdown from the 30-minute high is 0.0, but that is the high itself and gives no protection.

Verdict: skip.
